122: And how much must one take care not to permit himself to tell others that he had some business with this and this man, and he robbed him or wronged him in this and this way, or that he insulted him or aggrieved him or shamed him and the like. And [he is forbidden to relate this] even if he knows in himself that he is not falsifying in what he says, and [it is forbidden] even if there are superadded to this all the other details of the aforementioned heter. For certainly his intent at the time of telling was not for "benefit" — that is, to publicize his friend's taint so that wrongdoers be shamed in the eyes of men so that they take heed not to emulate their evil ways, or so that he himself see men spurning him, so that he thereby repent of his [own] evil ways. But his intent is only to shame him in the eyes of men, to make him an object of scorn and shame before them for having "touched" his money or his honor. And the more he sees that his words are accepted by the hearers and that he is thereby made an object of aversion and shame in their eyes, the more he rejoices and finds pleasure in this.
